rows.speaker: أبو بكر التونسي
rows.claim: Al-Tunisi transmits a consensus among every religious community's scholars that God began each revealed book with the basmala.
rows.anchor: نقل العلامة أبو بكر التونسي إجماع علماء كل ملة على أن الله تعالى أفتتح كل كتاب بها

rows.speaker: السيوطي عن السرميني
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti, as quoted by al-Sarmīnī, reports that the basmala opens every book; al-Sarmīnī takes the formula as particular to this community.
rows.anchor: وروى السيوطي فيما نقله عنه السرميني والعهدة عليه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فاتحة كل كتاب

rows.speaker: السرميني
rows.claim: Al-Sarmīnī infers particularity from reports that the written formula changed from bismika Allahumma to the complete basmala as revelations arrived.
rows.anchor: كان يكتب باسمك اللهم إلى أن نزل بسم الله مجراها فأمر بكتابة بسم الله

rows.speaker: السرميني
rows.claim: Al-Sarmīnī argues that if the nested meanings of Qur'an, Fatiha, and basmala belonged to earlier books, their meanings would be in every book, which is false.
rows.anchor: معاني الكتب في القرآن ومعانيه في الفاتحة ومعانيها في البسملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi answers that the staged commands do not prove earlier books lacked the formula, since its use then may simply have been unknown.
rows.anchor: أن الأمر بذلك التفصيل لا يستلزم النفي لإحتمال نفي العلم إذ ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the Qur'an's distinctive feature is the Arabic wording in this order; earlier scriptures were non-Arabic and Qur'anic quotations from them are translations.
rows.anchor: المختص بالقرآن اللفظ العربي بهذا الترتيب والكتب السماوية بأسرها خلافا للغيطي غير عربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi notes that the report that the formula opened every book itself weighs against claiming it was exclusive to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: على أن في أول الدليلين بظاهره دليلا على عدم الخصوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported position says the basmala is not a verse of any sura.
rows.anchor: إنها ليست آية من السور أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second position counts the basmala as a verse of every sura except Bara'a.
rows.anchor: أنها آية من جميعها غير براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third position counts it as a verse of the Fatiha alone.
rows.anchor: أنها آية من الفاتحة دون غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth position treats it only as a portion of a verse in the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: أنها بعض آية منها فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth position makes it an independent verse revealed to mark sura openings and separate suras, for blessing.
rows.anchor: آية فذة أنزلت لبيان رؤس السور تيمنا وللفصل بينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth position says repeated revelation made the basmala both a verse and, on other occasions, not a verse.
rows.anchor: يجوز جعلها آية منها وغير آية لتكرر نزولها بالوصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventh position treats it as part of a verse in every sura.
rows.anchor: أنها بعض آية من جميع السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An eighth position makes it a full verse in the Fatiha but only part of verses in other suras.
rows.anchor: أنها آية من الفاتحة وجزء آية من السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ninth position reverses the eighth: it is part of a Fatiha verse and a full verse elsewhere.
rows.anchor: عكسه ( العاشر ( أنها آيات فذة وإن أنزلت مرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tenth position counts it as a distinct verse repeatedly revealed.
rows.anchor: أنها آيات فذة وإن أنزلت مرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Mubarak, Meccans including Ibn Kathir, Kufans including Asim and al-Kisa'i, most Shafi'is, and Imamis hold it is a verse in all suras except Bara'a.
rows.anchor: فابن عباس وابن المبارك وأهل مكة كابن كثير وأهل الكوفة كعاصم والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the fifth position, that the basmala is an independent verse marking sura beginnings, is the well-known Hanafi doctrine.
rows.anchor: ومنهم أبو عمرو ويعقوب على الخامس وهو المشهور من مذهبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Shafi'is, Hamza, and a view attributed to Ahmad count it as a verse of the Fatiha alone.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الشافعية وحمزة ونسب للإمام أحمد بالثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinese including Malik, Syrians including al-Awza'i, and Basrans including Abu Amr and Ya'qub follow the fifth position.
rows.anchor: وأهل المدينة ومنهم مالك والشام ومنهم الأوزاعي والبصرة ومنهم أبو عمرو ويعقوب على الخامس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi explains his shift from Shafi'i sympathies to Hanafi doctrine and undertakes to defend his school against Fakhr al-Razi's sixteen proofs that the basmala is a Fatiha verse.
rows.anchor: فصرت مشغولا بأقوال السادة الحنفية وأقمت منها برياض شقائق النعمان

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: A report attributed to Umm Salama has the Prophet count the basmala as the first Fatiha verse and the following phrases as the next verses.
rows.anchor: عن أم سلمة أنها قالت قرأ رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فاتحة الكتاب فعد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that the Fatiha has seven verses, beginning with the basmala.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : فاتحة الكتاب سبع آيات أولاهن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Musa, through his son Abu Burda, reports the Prophet identifying the basmala as the special verse not given to anyone after Solomon and asking about the prayer's opening.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بردة عن أبيه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعلى عليه وسلم ألا أخبرك بآية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Jabir says the Prophet instructed him to say the basmala when beginning prayer.
rows.anchor: عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جابر بن عبدالله أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال له كيف تقول إذا قمت إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited the basmala before al-Hamdu lillah in prayer.
rows.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كان يقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Al-Thalabi reports that Ali began each sura in prayer with the basmala and said omitting it meant losing a verse.
rows.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه كان إذا أفتتح السورة في الصلاة يقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وكان يقول من ترك قراءتها فقد نقص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the seventh of the seven oft-repeated verses as the basmala.
rows.anchor: قال فاتحة الكتاب فقيل لابن عباس فأين السابعة فقال بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet's instruction not to omit the basmala because it is one of the Fatiha's verses.
rows.anchor: وبإسناده عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال إذا قرأتم أم القرآن فلا تدعوا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The prayer-splitting hadith has God call the worshipper's basmala a glorification of Him.
rows.anchor: قال يقول الله عز وجل قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فإذا قال بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال الله تعالى مجدني عبدي

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra recounts that the Prophet called a prayer cut short when a worshipper began without the basmala, and said omitting it invalidated the prayer.
rows.anchor: إذ دخل رجل يصلي فأفتتح الصلاة وتعوذ ثم قال الحمد لله رب العالمين فسمع النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: طلحة بن عبيدالله
rows.claim: Talha's report says omitting the basmala is equivalent to leaving a verse of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: عن طلحة بن عبيدالله قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من ترك بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فقد ترك آية من كتاب الله

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi argues that the command to read in God's name and the meaningful ba make reciting the basmala obligatory, hence part of the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: قراءة بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم واجبة في أول الفاتحة وإذا كان كذلك وجب أن تكون آية منها

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi argues that its inscription in Qur'anic script, unlike sura names and divisions, proves it is Qur'an.
rows.anchor: التسمية مكتوبة بخط القرآن وكل ما ليس من القرآن فإنه غير مكتوب بخط القرآن

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi argues that the basmala must be God's speech because it occurs between the covers of the Qur'an, which Muslims agree contains God's speech.
rows.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على أن ما بين الدفتين كلام الله تعالى والبسملة موجودة بينهما

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi begins his eighth proof by noting that most count the Fatiha as seven verses, then introduces disagreement over the count.
rows.anchor: أطبق الأكثرون على أن الفاتحة سبع آيات إلا أن الشافعي

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi argues that obligatory basmala recitation before the Fatiha, following the Prophet, makes it part of the sura.
rows.anchor: قراءة التسمية قبل الفاتحة واجبة فوجب كونها آية منها

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi invokes the hadith that an important matter begun without God's name is cut off to argue prayer without the basmala is defective.
rows.anchor: كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ فيه باسم الله فهو أبتر وأعظم الأعمال بعد الإيمان الصلاة

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi argues that the Prophet called the basmala the Qur'an's greatest verse, so it must be a complete verse in the Fatiha rather than only in al-Naml.
rows.anchor: ما أعظم آية في القرآن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فصدقه النبي في قوله

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi cites the report that companions challenged Mu'awiya for omitting the basmala in a public prayer and he repeated it aloud.
rows.anchor: أن معاوية قدم المدينة فصلى بالناس صلاة جهرية فقرأ أم القرآن ولم يقرأ البسملة

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi argues that earlier prophets began good works with God's name, so Muhammad and his followers should do likewise, citing the commands to follow their guidance and the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أن سائر الأنبياء كانوا عند الشروع في أعمال الخير يبتدؤن باسم الله

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi reasons that God, being eternal, should be mentioned before created beings; the required precedence supports reciting the basmala as a Fatiha verse.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى قديم والغير محدث فوجب بحكم المناسبة العقلية أن يكون ذكره سابقا

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi argues that because the basmala is Qur'an in al-Naml and appears repeatedly in Qur'anic script, it is Qur'an wherever repeated.
rows.anchor: لا شك أنها من القرآن في سورة النمل ثم إنا نراه مكررا بخط القرآن

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi uses the report that the Prophet wrote bismika Allahumma to argue that the complete formula belongs to the Qur'an and cannot be excluded.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام كان يكتب باسمك اللهم الحديث وهو يدل على أن أجزاء هذه الكلمة كلها من القرآن

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi says repeated revelation and the Prophet's instruction to write the formula in the muṣḥaf, together with precautionary hadith, require accepting its recitation and handling rulings.
rows.anchor: ثبت بالتواتر أن الله تعالى كان ينزل هذه الكلمة على محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Razi's proofs do not establish Fatiha membership: the Hanafi position accepts the basmala as an independent Qur'anic verse, and many Hanafis require its prayer recitation.
rows.anchor: أن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية مستقلة وهي من القرآن وإن لم تكن من الفاتحة نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reports the relied-upon Hanafi view that the basmala is required in a rak'a where recitation is required, citing al-Zayla'i and al-Zahidi.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزيلعي في شرح الكنز أن الأصح أنها واجبة وذكر الزاهدي عن المجتبي أن الصحيح أنها واجبة

rows.speaker: إبن وهبان
rows.claim: Ibn Wahban says that if someone forgetfully omits the basmala in every rakaa, prostration of forgetfulness is due.
rows.anchor: وقال إبن وهبان في منظومته ولو لم يبسمل ساهيا كل ركعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi presents Razi's eighth proof: Shafii counts the basmala, while Abu Hanifa counts sirat alladhina anamta alayhim; Razi calls the Hanafi count weak and says seven verses require the basmala.
rows.anchor: قال بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية وأبو حنيفة قال : إنها ليست آية لكن صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Razi's description of the Hanafi position as neglecting the basmala is extreme partisanship, since many Hanafis require it and he personally adopts the cautious view.
rows.anchor: فيسجد إذ إيجابها قال الأكثر وفي غنية المتملي وهو الأحوط وبه أقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi objects to Razi's Umm Salama proof: Abu Mulayka is not shown to have heard from her, and the quoted wording is not established among well-known versions, likely being paraphrase.
rows.anchor: بأن أبا مليكة لم يثبت سماعه عن أم سلمة وبتقديره للمعاصرة يقال إن هذا اللفظ لم يوجد في المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari and al-Bayhaqi report that the Prophet paused verse by verse, beginning with the basmala.
rows.anchor: وابن الأنباري والبيهقي كان إذا قرأ قطع قراءته آية آية يقول بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari and al-Bayhaqi also report the Prophet pausing verse by verse, beginning with the basmala.
rows.anchor: وابن الأنباري والبيهقي كان إذا قرأ قطع قراءته آية آية يقول بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Khuzayma and al-Hakim transmit a count that treats the basmala as one verse and al-Hamdu lillah as the next; Alusi says it still does not prove Fatiha membership.
rows.anchor: وابن خزيمة والحاكم بلفظ أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قرأ في الصلاة بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فعدها آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni reports that the Prophet counted verse by verse, counted the basmala, but did not count alayhim separately.
rows.anchor: والدارقطني بلفظ كان يقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين آلى آخرها قطعها آية آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the first two pause reports illustrate recitation practice and prove only that the basmala is a Qur'anic verse, not that it belongs to the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يقال عنت بهما بيان كيفية قراءة رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لسائر القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ibn Khuzayma version counts the basmala as the Qur'an's first verse and al-Hamdu lillah as its second, without specifying the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وهي الآية الأولى من القرآن والآية الثانية منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Daraqutni version may describe occasional recitation; it counts the formula because it is obligatory in prayer and deserves attention, not because it is textually part of the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: ولا دوام ولا وضعا ولا استعمالا من كتاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reads the stopping after an'amta alayhim as a complete meaning; stopping before ghayri'l-maghdubi would leave a phrase syntactically incomplete, and no separate count of alayhim is required.
rows.anchor: ومن أنعم الله تعالى عليه وعرف الذين ( أنعمت عليهم ) وجده تاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says matching verse lengths and end-rhymes is desirable but not required, and separating a described word from its qualification across verses has precedent.
rows.anchor: فإن تقارب الآي في الطول والقصر كتقارب الفقرات شيء مرغوب فيه وعدم التشابه في المقاطع لا يضر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi transmit Abu Hurayra's report that the Fatiha has seven verses, with the basmala one of them.
rows.anchor: أخرجه الطبراني وإبن مردويه والبيهقي بلفظ الحمد لله رب العالمين سبع آيات بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إحداهن

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni's version commands reciting the basmala before al-Hamd and calls the basmala one of the Fatiha's verses.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه الدارقطني بلفظ إذا قرأتم الحمد فأقرؤا بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إنها أم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi interprets the first Abu Hurayra wording as seven verses from al-Hamdu lillah to the end, while the basmala is one Qur'anic verse; his reading preserves the Hanafi view.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الرواية الأولى الحمد لله رب العالمين آلى آخر الآيات سبع آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi construes Abu Hurayra's wording as a rhetorical clarification that the basmala is one Qur'anic verse, not one of the Fatiha's verses; the report's opening can retain its literal sense on this reading.
rows.anchor: بسم الله الرحمن الرحمن الرحيم إحداهن أي مثل إحداهن في كونها آية من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the second wording as telling readers to recite the basmala before the Fatiha; its description of the Fatiha as the seven oft-repeated verses motivates reciting it.
rows.anchor: إذا أردتم قراءة الحمد إلى آخر ما يليه فأقراؤا قبله بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi accepts Razi's third proof only for the basmala's Qur'anic status, a point Hanafis do not dispute.
rows.anchor: فليس سوى آثبات أن التسمية من القرآن كما أقر هو به ولسنا ممن نخالفه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says several reports in Razi's fourth argument are weak and in any case do not establish that the basmala is part of the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: الحديث الأول الثاني والثالث والسادس مع ضعفه والثامن لا تدل على المقصود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The statement identifying the Fatiha's seventh verse as the basmala is Ibn Abbas's own, not necessarily a Prophetic report; he may have reasoned that an independent Qur'anic verse belongs in the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: والرابع موقوف على إبن عباس ولا نسلم أن حكمه الرفع لجواز الاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi allows that Ibn Abbas may have based the identification on Prophetic instruction as he understood it, without thereby asserting the basmala is a portion of the sura.
rows.anchor: أو نقول إنه قال ذلك أيضا عن توقيف لكن على ظنه واجتهاده أنه توقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi doubts the fifth report's wording and says it may be the version transmitted by al-Daraqutni; he does not rely on al-Razi for hadith and lacks al-Thalabi's text to check it.
rows.anchor: والخامس لي شك في صحته بهذا اللفظ ولعله باللفظ الذي خرجه به الدارقطني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi calls the seventh prayer-interruption report fabricated in style and says its missing chain and absence from Shafi'i's leading proofs further undermine it.
rows.anchor: والسابع لا تلوح عليه طلاوة كلام رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ولا فصاحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Razi's fifth argument wrongly infers Fatiha membership from the obligation to recite the basmala and misuses the command in al-Alaq.
rows.anchor: ففيها أنا لا نسلم أن وجوبها في أول الفاتحة مستلزم لكونها آية منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi calls inscription in Qur'anic script the strongest proof that the basmala is Qur'an, but says it does not prove that it is part of the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: فهو أقوى ما يستدل به على كون البسملة من القرآن وأما على أنها من الفاتحة فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says denying the basmala's Qur'anic status because it is written in the muṣḥaf is intellectually unsound and contrary to fairness and faith.
rows.anchor: وتعرض نفاة كونها قرآنا للتكلم في هذا الدليل مما لا يرضاه الطبع السليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Razi's seventh proof works for Hanafis, since they too accept that the text between the covers includes the basmala as Qur'an.
rows.anchor: الحجة السابعة فلنا لا علينا كما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says Razi's eighth proof depends on first proving Abu Hanifa's verse division weak, a claim Alusi regards as formidable to establish.
rows.anchor: فدون إثبات مدارها وهو توهين كلام مولانا أبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى جبال راسيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against Razi's ninth proof, Alusi notes that the prayer is already opened by the takbir and intention; applying the hadith to every consequential act would also require basmala before bowing and prostration.
rows.anchor: لأن الفاتحة جزء من الصلاة المفتتحة بالتكبير المقارن للنية الذي هو ركن منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi extends the reductio: if every prayer movement needs a basmala to avoid being cut off, Razi would have to recite it before bowing, prostrating, and every transition.
rows.anchor: وسائر إنتقالاته رحمة الله تعالى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's tenth argument does not establish a Fatiha verse against Hanafis, since Alusi has already explained their doctrine.
rows.anchor: الحجة العاشرة فلا تقوم علينا لأنا أعلمناك بمذهبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mu'awiya report, even if accepted, could show only that he omitted an obligatory basmala and repeated the prayer; the companions may have waited to see whether prostration of forgetfulness repaired the lapse.
rows.anchor: أن معاوية لما لم يقرأ البسملة وترك الواجب ولم يسجد للسهو أعاد الصلاة لتقع سليمة من الخلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another version says Mu'awiya omitted the takbir at bowing and prostration too, so repeating the prayer does not prove basmala membership in the Fatiha; whether he recited aloud remains unclear.
rows.anchor: ولم يكبر عند الخفض إلى الركوع والسجود فلما سلم ناداه المهاجرون والأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Razi's appeal to following earlier prophets misreads Qur'anic exegesis and Prophetic reports, and obligation still would not prove that the basmala is part of the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: ففيها كما تقدم أن الوجوب لا يستلزم الجزئية على أن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi dismisses Razi's thirteenth proof and says the remaining arguments cannot establish the disputed point.
rows.anchor: فلا تجديه نفعا في مقابلتنا أيضا وفيها ما في أخواتها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Muslim's sound report from Abu Hurayra divides prayer between God and servant: three Fatiha verses for God, the middle verse shared, and three for the servant, beginning with al-Hamdu lillah.
rows.anchor: أخرج مسلم وغيره من حديث أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقول قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers this stronger Muslim report over al-Thalabi's versions: its seven-verse count starts with al-Hamdu lillah and leaves the basmala outside the Fatiha, while not denying its Qur'anic status.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن البسملة ليست من الفاتحة وأنها سبع بدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects objections based on al-Ala's criticism by Ibn Ma'in because many critics authenticated him; a solitary less-trusted variation is anomalous, not a balanced contradiction.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن مدار الرواية العلاء وقد ضعفه إبن معين فهو على جلالة الرجل لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects reading half as a semantic class or category, since the report's explicit counting and division of verses makes such metaphor unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وحمل النصف فيه على النصف في المعنى أو الصنف من عدم الإنصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the prayer division cannot concern only a portion that also includes actions and an appended sura; its halves must form a coherent whole.
rows.anchor: وكون المراد بعض قراءة الصلاة إذ الظاهر لا يمكن أن يراد لوجود الأعمال وضم السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra's report says al-Kawthar has three verses and al-Mulk thirty, without counting a basmala at the start of either sura.
rows.anchor: وقد نص صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فيما رواه أبو هريرة عنه بأن الأولى ثلاث آيات والثانية ثلاثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi challenges proponents to explain why an independent basmala would not add to these counts, or why a basmala counted as part of a sura was not counted.
rows.anchor: ولو عدها مستقلة لزاد العدد أو جزءا لورد وعلى المثبت البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects Razi's analogy to a phrase that is a verse in one place and part of a verse elsewhere: that other phrase has a reason to be partial, while this basmala does not.
rows.anchor: بعيد بل قياس باطل لوجود المقتضى للجزئية هناك وإنتفائه هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many suras were revealed without a basmala and received it later; the sound report about the beginning of revelation supports that it is not a verse of those suras.
rows.anchor: نزل الكثير من السور بلا بسملة ثم ضمت بعد وحديث الصحيح في بدء الوحي يبدي صحة ما قلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the basmala was the first revelation is weak; even if it came first, that would not prove it belongs to a sura.
rows.anchor: وحديث أنها أول ما نزلت ليس بالقوي بل الثابت ويشكل عليه ما روى أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكتب بأسمك اللهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi's conclusion is that the basmala is an independent Qur'anic verse, not a part of any sura, and its recitation is obligatory rather than merely recommended.
rows.anchor: فهي آية من القرآن مستقلة ولا ينبغي لمن وقف على الأحاديث أن يتوقف في قرآنيتها أو ينكر وجوب قراءتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He regards it as implausible that Abu Hanifa would leave this major prayer issue without an explicit ruling; the valid report from him supports obligation.
rows.anchor: والقول بأنه لم ينص بشيء ليس بشيء وكيف لا ينص إلى آخر عمره في مثل هذا الأمر الخطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says concealing the basmala in aloud prayers does not make it merely recommended; the Prophet and early caliphs recited it quietly.
rows.anchor: والأخفاء بها في الجهرية لا يدل على السنية فإن القول بوجوبها لا ينافي إخفاءها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet did not recite the basmala aloud before his death.
rows.anchor: فعن إبن عباس لم يجهر النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بالبسملة حتى مات

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that he did not hear the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, or Uthman reciting the basmala aloud; Alusi says this does not deny quiet recitation.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم عن أنس صليت خلف النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وأبي بكر وعمر وعثمان فلم اسمع منهم أحدا يقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reports that a father rebuked his son for reciting the basmala aloud, saying the Prophet and first caliphs began aloud with al-Hamdu lillah; Alusi understands the formula to have been recited quietly.
rows.anchor: قال : سمعني أبي وأنا أقول بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فقال أي بني إياك والحدث في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi lists many authorities for silent recitation, including al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn al-Zubayr, Ammar, major Successors, and Ahmad.
rows.anchor: وهو مذهب الثوري وابن المبارك وابن مسعود وابن الزبير وعمار بن ياسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says only Ibn Abbas's report explicitly supports loud recitation; it conflicts with earlier reports or may describe occasional public demonstration that the basmala is recited.
rows.anchor: وأحاديث الجهر لم يصح منها سوى حديث إبن عباس الذي أخرجه الشافعي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some hadith specialists say every explicit report of loud basmala recitation has a flaw in its chain; al-Daraqutni reportedly said no sound report establishes it.
rows.anchor: روى عن بعض الحفاظ ليس حديث صريح في الجهر إلا وفي إسناده مقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the claim that Anas's conflicting versions arose from Umayyad hostility to Ali: the strongest chain favors silence, and accusing its transmitters of lying is less plausible than accusing Anas and the Companions.
rows.anchor: إذ يقدم عند التعارض الأقوى إسنادا وهو هنا ما يوافقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls al-Razi's suggestion of political intimidation strange, asking why the Medinan Companions would publicly accuse Mu'awiya if they feared him.
rows.anchor: كيف يبدي إحتمال التهمة ويروى إعتراض أهل المدينة على سيد ملوك بني أمية

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi's first proof of loud recitation is that a basmala belonging to the sura should share its public or quiet recitation; Alusi answers that it is not part of the sura and parts may differ in volume regardless.
rows.anchor: أن البسملة من السورة فحكمها حكمها سرا وجهرا

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi's second argument says the basmala is praise and glorification and therefore should be spoken aloud, citing the command to remember God intensely.
rows.anchor: أنها ثناء وتعظيم فوجب الإعلان بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi replies that most prayer phrases also praise and glorify God, so this argument would absurdly require reciting all of them aloud.
rows.anchor: ويرده أن غالب مشتملات الصلاة كذلك أفيجهر بها

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi's third argument says loud remembrance publicly shows pride in God and disregard for those who object, and calls this proof firmly convincing to him.
rows.anchor: إن الجهر بذكر الله يدل عى ألإفتخار به وعدم المبالاة بمنكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says this does not explain why other glorifications in bowing and prostration should be hidden; he cites poetry on the hidden Night of Decree and concealed nobles to show hiddenness is no disgrace.
rows.anchor: فليلة القدر تخفي وتلك خير الليالي وياليت شعري أكان تسبيحه الله تعالى في ركوعه وسجوده

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi's fourth proof is the report that the Companions challenged Mu'awiya after he omitted the basmala in prayer.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه الشافعي عن أنس أن معاوية صلى بأهل المدينة ولم يقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says this report is countered by the reports of silent recitation, or the Companions may have inferred omission from other signs without hearing the prayer.
rows.anchor: ويرده معارضوه أو يقال لم يقرأ على ظاهره وعلموا ذلك ببعض القرائن

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi's fifth proof cites a Bayhaqi report of the Prophet reciting the basmala aloud, also attributed to Umar, his son, Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Ali, and says following Ali is guidance.
rows.anchor: ما روى البيهقي عن أبي هريرة كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجهر في الصلاة ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says these reports are contradicted, and any loud recitation could have been occasional for teaching; he denies Sunni recognition of tawatur from Ali and criticizes Shi'i claims that all their attributions are mutawatir.
rows.anchor: وما زعم من تواتر نسبته إلى علي ممنوع عند أهل السنة نعم أدعته الشيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Sunni practice ordinarily follows the two senior caliphs and cites reports successively urging the Companions, the rightly guided caliphs, then Abu Bakr and Umar as guides.
rows.anchor: على أن الشائع عند أهل السنة تقديم ما عليه الشيخان وإذا أختلفا فما عليه الصديق

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Razi's sixth argument says the basmala implies beginning with God's aid, reminds people that obedience depends on God's power, and makes audible recitation an act of commanding right.
rows.anchor: متعلقة بفعل مضمر نحو بإعانة بسم الله أشرعوا ولا شك أن إستماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi lists proposed meanings of ba in the basmala: seeking aid, accompaniment, attachment, superiority, redundancy, and oath; he rejects the last four.
rows.anchor: فالباء إما للإستعانة أو المصاحبة أو الألصاق أو الأستعلاء أو زائدة أو قسمية

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi's wording favors construing ba as seeking God's assistance, which makes His name seem essential to the act.
rows.anchor: فالذي يشعر به كلام البيضاوي أرجحية الأول وأيد بأن جعله للإستعانة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's wording favors accompaniment: this usage is more common, conveys blessing and reverence, rebuts idolaters' invocation, and implies God's name accompanies every part of the act.
rows.anchor: وما يدل عليه كلام الزمخشري أرجحية الثاني وأيد بأن باء المصاحبة أكثر في الإستعمال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also adduces the report that God's naming is in every Muslim's heart whether or not it is spoken, and the hadith about God's name protecting from harm.
rows.anchor: ويناسبه ما روى في الحديث تسمية الله تعالى في قلب كل مسلم يسمى أو لم يسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers assistance as nearly necessary: it expresses humility and dependence, rejects independent human power, opens mercy, and fits the Fatiha's appeal for help and the command to read in God's name.
rows.anchor: أن الإستعانة أولى بل يكاد أن تكون متعينة إذ فيها من الأدب والإستكانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that assistance treats God's name as a debased tool: reliance on God is valid and Qur'an itself commands seeking His help.
rows.anchor: وليست كل إستعانة بآلة ممتهنة ولا شك في صحة أستعنت بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi calls the hidden imperative parsing awkward and unsupported; reflecting on the Fatiha's direct statement of worship and reliance conveys far more without that difficulty.
rows.anchor: أن إنفهام الأمر بالمعروف من هذه الجملة يحتاج إلى فكر لو صرف عشر معشاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi argues that polytheists seek help from their gods as intermediaries, making the instrument analogy more apt for their practice than the accompaniment analogy.
rows.anchor: فلأن المشركين إلى الإستعانة بآلهتهم أقرب إذ هم وسائطهم في التقرب إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An instrument must persist through every part of an action, but accompaniment need not; the report about God's naming better suits assistance because it teaches reliance on God's power.
rows.anchor: فلأن الآلة لا بد من وجودها في كل جزء إلى آخر الفعل وإلا لم يتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessing does not uniquely follow from accompaniment: if inferred from context it can equally attend instrumental reliance, and Alusi denies that blessing is the inherent meaning of accompaniment.
rows.anchor: فلأنه إن أراد أن معنى المصاحبة التبرك فظاهر البطلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi denies that God's name cannot be an instrument if the basmala is part of a sura; opening a work does not prevent a phrase from being its part.
rows.anchor: فلأن ما يفتتح به الشيء لا مانع من كونه جزءا فالفاتحة مفتتح القرآن وجزؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the hadith about God's name preventing harm as invoking God's aid and protection; even alternative readings about accompanying benefit are only supporting indications, and many indications also favor assistance.
rows.anchor: فلأن معنى الحديث أفعل كذا مستعينا بإسم الله الذي لا يضرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi speculates that al-Zamakhshari may avoid assistance because Mu'tazili doctrine gives human beings independent agency; he promises to address that theology later.
rows.anchor: ويمكن على بعد أن يكون عدم إختيار الزمخشري لها لنزعات الشيطان الإعتزالية من إستقلال العبد بفعله

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir supplies the omitted verb as I recite, since what is recited is the object; Alusi says each speaker supplies the specific action they are beginning, a natural convention that permits basmala to begin the full act.
rows.anchor: فذهب الإمام إبن جرير إلى تقديره أتلو لأن تاليه متلو

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra, with a report from Ibn Abbas, prefers an imperative addressed to people to begin in God's name, because God placed the basmala first to urge this practice.
rows.anchor: جعل المقدر فعل أمر متوجه إلى العباد ليتحد قائل الملفوظ والمقدر وأختاره الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians generally estimate a broad verb such as I begin; Alusi gives three reasons: applicability to any basmala, direct fulfillment of its purpose, and alignment with the hadith about matters begun without God's name.
rows.anchor: وذهب النحويون إلى تقديره عاما نحو أبتديء وأيد بوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers Ibn Jarir's specific recitation verb because it makes the whole recitation occur with God's assistance, whereas beginning only links the formula to the initial moment.
rows.anchor: وما ذهب إليه الإمام أمس وأخص بالمقصود وأتم شمولا فإنه يقتضي أن القراءة واقعة بكمالها مقرونة بالتسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says grammarians' use of general being or stability as examples does not prove a general verb belongs here, since those are illustrative examples where no specific governor is intended.
rows.anchor: فليس بجيد لأنهم فعلوه تمثيلا حيث لا يقصدون عاملا بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says beginning here is specifically the beginning of recitation, not a generic action; the basmala itself already makes the reciter a beginner, so no hidden act is needed to establish that.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد به إبتداء القراءة وهو أخص من القراءة لصدقها على قراءة الأول والوسط والآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the formula itself begins the work without an elided verb; the hadith does not require every important act to contain an explicit or implied verb.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد الحديث بأن كل أمر ذي بال لم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the dispute is between a general verb like begin and a specific verb like recite, so arguments against recite alone do not settle which estimate is stronger.
rows.anchor: وأيضا البحث إنما هو في ترجيح تقدير الفعل العام كأبدأ أو أشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some estimate a noun such as my beginning, but this requires an additional omitted predicate; the noun's static meaning also competes with the contextually apt ongoing aspect of a present-tense verb.
rows.anchor: وذهب البعض إلى تقدير إبتدائي مثلا وفيه زيادة إضمار لوجوب إضمار الخبر حينئذ

rows.speaker: ابن عربي
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi interprets the phrase esoterically as the predicate of an omitted subject, the world's beginning and manifestation through divine names, and Alusi says objecting to him is unfair.
rows.anchor: وجعل الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره هذا الجار خبر مبتدأ مضمر هو إبتداء العالم وظهوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many prefer estimating the verb after the basmala because God's name precedes the act in essence; Alusi links this to an a priori proof and cites a gnostic who sees God before every thing.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العارفين ما رأيت شيئا إلا ورأيت الله قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says preposing God's name can sever claims of self-power and makes sense for the messenger's mission, while the first revelation preposes the verb because its context was prophethood rather than disputation or public preaching.
rows.anchor: وظهر سر تقديم الفعل في أول آية نزلت إذ المقام إذ ذاك مقام نبوة ولا رد ولا تبليغ فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers estimating a preceding verb: putting it after ba, ism, Allah, or the attributes would split grammatical units or make mercy appear an exclusive cause of recitation.
rows.anchor: وعندي هنا يقدر مقدما وبه قال الأكثرون وإن تقديره مؤخرا مؤخر عن ساحة التحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a preceding verb, the formula still implies restriction: one reads with God's help or blessing because He is the Merciful, excluding those outside that stated cause in this rhetorical context.
rows.anchor: أقرأ مستعينا أو متبركا بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم لأنه الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi offers a mystical reading: mentally the created act precedes its omission in speech, while only God's pre-eternal name appears, hinting at the fixed archetypes in divine knowledge and God's absolute priority.
rows.anchor: رمز خفي إلى تقديم الأعيان الثابتة في العلم وإن لم يكن على وجود الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some gnostics say they see God in everything without believing in indwelling; Alusi calls this a higher rank than seeing God before things and mentions four spiritual ranks.
rows.anchor: قال ما رأيت شيئا إلا ورأيت الله تعالى فيه ولا حلول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars use mustaqirr and laghw differently for an adverbial phrase: by whether its governor is expressed, whether it is a general implied verb, or whether its governor is outside or understood from the phrase.
rows.anchor: والظرف مستقر عند بعض ولغو عند آخرين وقد أختلف في تفسيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the terminology is conventional, Alusi adopts the distinction that makes this phrase mustaqirr regardless of the estimated verb.
rows.anchor: وحيث لا مشاحة فيه إختار الأول فيكون الظرف هنا مستقرا كيفما قدر العامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians explain the ba's kasra as a compromise: particles tend toward light, often-used fatha, but ba's particle status favors kasra and its genitive effect matches that vowel.
rows.anchor: إلا أنها من حيث كونها كلمات برأسها مظنة للإبتداء وهو بالساكن متعذر أو متعسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation distinguishes ba from conjunction waw and comparative kaf, which have only one relevant feature, while oath waw and ta borrow their genitive function from the original ba.
rows.anchor: ولا نقض بواو العطف اللازمة للحرفية ولا بكاف التشبيه اللازمة للجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says these grammatical rationales were devised after the fact merely to suggest a fitting pattern, so they cannot bear forceful scrutiny.
rows.anchor: وهذه علل نحوية مستخرجة بعد الوقوع لإبداء مناسبة فلا تتحمل مناقشة لضعفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A symbolic interpreter says the kasra of the basmala's ba teaches that divine knowledge is reached through humility and servitude; Ibn al-Farid's verse makes lowering a cause of elevation by God's gift, not human stratagem.
rows.anchor: كسرت الباء في البسملة تعليما للتوصل إلى الله تعالى والتعلق بأسمائه بكسر الجناب والخضوع

rows.speaker: ابن الفارض
rows.claim: Ibn al-Farid's poem says that a lowered point of ba can raise the seeker beyond what effort could attain, provided one recognizes one's own humility and dependence.
rows.anchor: ولو كنت لي من نقطة الباء خفضة رفعت إلى ما لم تنله بحيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi limits this symbolism to the ba of the basmala and says it cannot be applied to every genitive ba.
rows.anchor: وهو أمر مخصوص بباء البسملة لا يمكن أن يجري في باء الجر مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi's own symbolism makes ba the second rank after the simple alif, a sign of true existence; he recalls al-Shibli saying he was the point beneath ba and quotes Ibn Arabi on its secret of servitude.
rows.anchor: وعندي في سر ذلك أن الباء هي المرتبة الثانية بالنسبة إلى الألف البسيطة المجردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because mercy precedes wrath, Alusi reads the genitive ba as a sign of divine beauty and mercy, with its kasra symbolizing humility and preparing the way for effusion.
rows.anchor: وللأولى السبق كما يشير إليه حديث سبقت رحمتي غضبي وباء الجر إشارة إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with ba hastens glad tidings and signifies that mercy is central; a hadith says no one enters Paradise by deeds alone, but only through God's mercy, even the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي الإبتداء بها هنا تعجيل للبشارة ورمز إلى أن المدار هو الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi links the basmala's ba to the Muhammadan reality and first determination, saying divine effusion came through the Prophet and citing reports that his light was created first and the cosmos for his sake.
rows.anchor: وأما إشارة إلى الحقيقة المحمدية والتعين الأول المشار إليه بقوله صلى الله علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's predominating quality was mercy, especially toward the believing community, as the Qur'an calls him a mercy to the worlds.
rows.anchor: ولكون الغالب عليه عليه الصلاة والسلام صفة الرحمة لا سيما على مؤمني الأمة
